Memorization in Bilinear Layers — experiment figures

Every figure from Parts 1–3 of the handoff, labeled for reference. Bilinear layer y = D((Lx) ∗ (Rx)); folded tensor T[i,j,c] = Σh D[c,h]·sym(L[h,i]R[h,j]); boolean inputs make diagonal entries act as linear terms (outlined cells in every heatmap). 5 seeds per trained result; figures display seed 0, cross-seed statistics live in results.md. All predictions committed to git before their measurements. Code: basis_aligned/memorization_post/part1.py, part2.py; matrices saved as .npy alongside each figure.

Part 1 (Dog/Cat/Catfish toy): F1 clean model · F2 trained vs clean · F3 diagonal logic · F4 undercomplete · F5 key Gram · F6 collateral (C1) · F7 discriminator · F8 path removal · F8b functional edit
Part 2 (100 random facts): F9 SGD vs construction · F9b D-sparsity sweep · F10 extraction · F11 unlearning · F12 margin bound
Part 3 (1200 facts, 2 blocks): F13 cross-layer verdict · F13b capacity vs width · F13c 2-layer edits · KKT methods box

Scaling note — compute in the CP basis, render in the third-order basis

The dense folded tensor T is d²·C entries — ~10⁹ (4 GB) at d_model = C = 1024, hopeless beyond. Nothing here needs it: the model’s own parameterization is a CP form of T with H components, T = Σh D[:,h] ⊗ L[h,:] ⊗ R[h,:], and every quantitative result has an exact factored equivalent. The dense format’s only role at scale is pedagogy: render d×d slices for the few classes you display.

  • Evaluation — the forward pass D((Lx)∗(Rx)), O(H(d+C)); never forms T.
  • Per-class slices & spectra (F1–F4, F7, F10, rank claims) — Bc = Lᵀdiag(D[c,:])R; rank ≤ live units in class c’s D-row. Exact eigen/SVD via the span of live L/R rows: orthonormalize a d×2s matrix, decompose the 2s×2s core.
  • Folded-tensor similarity (F9) — CP inner-product identity ⟨T₁,T₂⟩ = Σh,h′ (D₁ᵀD₂)∘(L₁L₂ᵀ)∘(R₁R₂ᵀ): three H×H Grams, O(H²(2d+C)); the symmetrized version adds one cross term (L₁R₂ᵀ)∘(R₁L₂ᵀ).
  • KKT edits / fact addition / unlearning (F6, F11, F8b) — a rank-1 input-space update is literally appending one hidden unit (L-row C⁻¹z*, R-row z*, D-column α·ec); C is d×d from keys only. Entry-level surgery (F8) is the same append with L-row ei, R-row ej. Repeated edits grow H by one each; recompress with a few ALS sweeps when it matters.
  • Gram, collateral, margin bound (F5, F6, F12) — keys and O(H) bilinear evaluations zkᵀBczj = D[c,:]·((Lzk)∗(Rzj)); no tensor.

The two things that genuinely do not scale are not tensor-format problems: the exhaustive 2ⁿ enumeration behind F12 (exponential in input bits; at scale the analytic Gram bound + sampling is the guarantee), and slice eigendecompositions when a D-row is fully dense (min(d,H)³ — still fine at d ≤ 4096).

Part 1 — the 3-class toy (Dog / Cat / Catfish)

Features [furry, happy, whiskers]; Dog = furry∧happy, Cat = furry∧whiskers, Catfish = whiskers∧happy. Overcomplete H=8, undercomplete H=2.

F1 Hand-coded clean model — one symmetric off-diagonal pair per class

The H=3 construction stores each class as exactly one interaction: Bc has 0.5 on its feature pair and nothing else. Verified: symmetric rank 2 with eigenvalues ±1/2 on (ea±eb)/√2, asymmetric L/R slice exactly rank 1. This is the reference every trained panel is compared against. Acceptance: pass.

F2 Trained H=8 vs clean (seed 0)

The pre-registered prediction confirmed on every seed: SGD uses the positive feature-pair interaction (+3.2 to +3.6) PLUS negative logic on the class's absent feature. (A weight-decay sweep {0, 10⁻³, 10⁻²} was trained too — it shrinks magnitudes but never changes the channel; stats in results.md.) Note the trained slices are messier than clean: the Dog slice is asymmetric rank 3, not rank 1 (surprise #2).

F3 The linear-logic-via-diagonal effect

Because x²=x on booleans, diagonal entries are linear terms. The largest single negative term in every trained class is the absent feature's diagonal (−3 to −4) — "not-whiskers" implemented linearly, dwarfing the noisy positive own-feature diagonals (which sign-flip across seeds, surprise #1).

F4 Undercomplete H=2 — mixed storage

With fewer hidden units than classes, interactions mix across classes; all 5 seeds still reach 100% accuracy but find visibly different solutions (folded-tensor cosine across seeds as low as 0.50). This is the regime where edits get dangerous — see F5/F6.

F5 The stored-key Gram matrix — the collateral-damage forecast

Cosines between hidden representations of the stored keys. Overcomplete: near-diagonal (mean |off-diag| 0.18). Undercomplete: heavy off-diagonal mass (mean 0.48, max 0.96). The off-diagonals are the standing prediction of which edits will bleed into which classes.

F6 Claim check C1 (centerpiece): predicted vs measured collateral

Gram-predicted collateral of every single-class KKT-to-uniform edit, committed to disk before measurement, against measured damage: Pearson r = 0.943, Spearman ρ = 0.931 over all 60 (edit, victim) pairs; per-regime r = 0.87 overcomplete / 0.93 undercomplete. Undercomplete collateral is ~4× larger (mean margin drop 6.0 vs 1.6). Acceptance: pass.

F7 The Dog-minus-Cat discriminator

T[:,:,Dog] − T[:,:,Cat] is effectively rank 2: "furry-and-happy, not whiskers" against "furry-and-whiskers". Also verified here: pulling out T[:,:,Dog] alone gives a standalone Dog detector that matches the full model exactly (max mismatch 6×10⁻¹⁵ over all 8 inputs); a two-class sub-model needs H=2.

F8 Path removal, tail redesign — the entry is not the path

Redesigned setup (no 4th class): features [furry, happy, whiskers, tail]; Dog = furry∧happy or happy∧tail, Cat = furry∧whiskers or whiskers∧tail, Catfish = whiskers∧happy. Goal: remove the (happy,tail)→Dog path without touching the other four keys — note the kept Cat(whiskers,tail) path shares tail with the removed one. Row 1: the minimal-norm edit zeroes the (happy,tail) entry exactly and preserves (furry,happy) exactly, yet the Dog(happy,tail) key is still classified Dog on 5/5 seeds. Row 2: even zeroing all four tail-involving entries of Dog’s slice does not flip it — the (happy,happy) diagonal, shared with the kept Dog path, alone outscores the competitors (registered 0.65-confidence prediction failed). Row 3: undercomplete, the same minimal edit bleeds (2/5 seeds flip non-target keys), and the full-tail edit is not even expressible (5 constraints > 3 free parameters). Whole-unit ablation is catastrophic in both regimes. Weight-basis surgery cannot remove this fact — see F8b.

F8b The functional key-frame edit removes the fact the tensor surgery couldn’t

The Part-2 KKT family brought back to the toy: a least-norm update to Dog’s D-row with constraints in the stored-key frame — set fDog(zhappy,tail) one logit below the best competitor, preserve fDog(zfurry,happy) exactly. Overcomplete: the target key flips on 5/5 seeds with zero collateral (kept-key margin delta exactly 0), while the (happy,tail) tensor entry stays visibly nonzero — behavior removed without zeroing the mechanistic entry. Undercomplete: the same edit flips the target 5/5 but drags Cat keys to Dog on 3/5 seeds (mean accuracy deltas −0.6/−0.6/−0.4 on Cat(f,w)/Cat(w,t)/Catfish). Collateral is a property of the regime (stored-key overlap, the F5 Gram), not of the edit. Registered predictions confirmed (both halves).

Part 2 — 100 random facts (20-bit keys → 10 classes)

Working point H*=40 (smallest H where both SGD and the ALS construction reach 100% memorization with exact interpolation). Edits use weights + fact list only, no corpus.

F9 SGD vs the closed-form construction — same family, not same point

Folded-tensor similarity SGD-vs-construction is 0.12 [0.09, 0.15] with BOTH required baselines at ~0 (random init and permuted-fact construction) — acceptance passes. But the honest reading is tempered by the agent's extra control: ALS-vs-ALS across re-inits is 0.07–0.13, the same range, and SGD-vs-SGD is 0.32. The exact-interpolation solution family is wide; SGD is as close to the construction as the construction is to itself. Panel iii's "D ≉ −I" is superseded by F9b.

F9b D column structure vs sparsity strength — Logan's −I, deconfounded

Follow-up to Logan's feedback that D does reach −I under sparsity as one of many solutions. Three findings: (1) F9's low dominance (0.39–0.49) averaged over all 40 columns including near-dead ones — restricted to live units, dominance is already 0.78–0.88 at the original L1=10⁻³ and rises to 0.87–0.95 at L1=10⁻¹, while live units collapse to 10–12 ≈ one per class (middle panel). The signed one-hot structure is real and strengthens with sparsity. (2) The sign is gauge in this parameterization — flipping Lh flips the product, L1 is invariant — and measured negative-dominant fractions sit at 0.25–0.75 around 0.5 at every strength, exactly as a sign gauge predicts. −I vs +I is unidentified here; the invariant statement is |D| → scaled class-permutation, with −I the representative under any sign-fixing convention. (3) Memorization stays 100% across the whole sweep.

F10 Extraction: facts are a joint code, not separable rank-1 pieces

Blind eigen-extraction of individual facts from folded class slices fails robustly: 0–1% recovery at every Gram-overlap bin, every seed, and H up to 400 (match score 0.52 = the typical inter-key overlap itself). Informed key-frame attribution (least-squares onto the C⁻¹-weighted key dictionary) partially succeeds — 44–51% vs 10% chance for SGD (96% for the pure KKT interpolant) — and degrades with overlap (0.61 → 0.43 across bins). The memorizing solutions carry large residuals off the key frame (operator norm 11–30, comparable to the slice eigenvalues).

F11 KKT unlearning of 10 facts — the closed-form prediction is exact

Editing 10 facts to uniform: forgetting exact (deviation < 10⁻⁹ on all 10, all 5 seeds), collateral on the 90 kept facts nearly nil (2 argmax flips out of 450 victim slots). The registered joint-KKT collateral prediction matches measurement at r = 1.000000 (max error 1.8×10⁻¹⁰); the cheaper pure-Gram proxy still ranks victims at Spearman 0.47. The naive baseline (subtract the fact's rank-1 component, no re-tensioning) is 9.2× worse on collateral, flips 249/450 victims, and fails to forget at all (cross-talk among its own 10 edits leaves deviation 23–68) — it fails in kind, not degree.

F12 The guarantee on all 2²⁰ inputs — the bound holds, margins are not small

Exhaustive enumeration of every one of the 1,048,576 inputs (6 s on CPU). Max off-fact-set margins: 12.2 (min-C-norm KKT interpolant), 33.5 (ALS), 63.3 (SGD) — versus minimum on-fact margins of 5.0/5.0/10.9, and ~20% of off-fact inputs exceed the min on-fact margin for ALS/SGD (1.4% for the interpolant). The analytic Gram bound 2·max|λ|·xᵀC⁻¹x (+ residual term) holds everywhere but is 35–55× loose. The claim the post can make is exactly the bound — not margin smallness, and the interpolant is by far the best-behaved off-distribution.

Surprises the post should quote

  • Part 1: own-feature diagonals appear with sign flips across seeds; the trained Dog slice is asymmetric rank 3, not the clean rank 1; interaction-zeroing alone does not behaviorally remove a path (diagonals co-carry it); unit-level surgery fails even overcomplete; the tiny dataset was never degenerate.
  • Part 2: F9's similarity acceptance is weaker than it looks (SGD is as close to the construction as the construction is to itself); D's −I structure is real but sign-gauged and visible only after excluding dead units (F9b); blind rank-1 fact extraction fails completely at all capacities; naive removal fails in kind (no forgetting); off-fact margins are large — only the bound survives as the guarantee.

Parts 3 (200 facts / 2 layers, cross-layer storage) and 4 (structure interpolation) pending. Repo: basis_aligned/memorization_post/ — results.md has every claim check with numbers, surprises.md the full list.

Part 3 — 1200 facts in 2 bilinear blocks with a residual stream

x → x + B1(x) → … + B2(…), linear readout, no biases; 20-bit keys, 10 classes; sized so ONE block fails but two suffice. Registered predictions P1–P4 in predictions/part3_predictions.md (committed before the sizing sweep). Sizing surprise: the handoff’s 200 facts is far below single-block capacity — one block memorizes 200, 400, even 800 facts at every width (a quadratic in 20 booleans has only ~210 monomials; margin classification is ~4× cheaper than interpolation). The ceiling is between 800 and 1200: at 1200 facts a single block saturates at 54.0% with H=40 and H=210 (the full quadratic span) identical — an expressivity limit, not a parameter limit. Two blocks at H=40 each (4,800 block parameters vs the failing single block’s 12,600) hold all 1200 at loss ≈ 0; H=120 holds 2000.

F13 Verdict: it IS cross-layer — the composed terms are the memory

Metric gate first: with one block frozen at zero, the attribution metric assigns 0 of 200 memorized facts to the dead layer (both directions) — the metric detects one-sided storage when it exists. On the real model: (i) the bins classify each fact by whether a SINGLE layer suffices: “either alone (redundant)” means layer 1 alone AND layer 2 alone each classify the fact; “needs both (composed)” means no single layer suffices — which is where cross-term storage lands. 62–66% of the 1200 facts need both layers, and every bin except “neither” sits at the 10% chance floor — essentially no fact is attributable to one layer (P1 confirmed, far beyond the predicted <30%). (ii) the degree-2 additive surrogate W(z + B1(z) + B2(z)) keeps only 17–19% of facts (loses ~980/1200); the median fact has ~98% of its logit magnitude in the composed degree-3/4 cross terms, and the cross-term margin contribution is almost entirely positive — the composed terms are not a correction, they ARE the memory (P2 confirmed at ~82% lost vs the predicted ≥25%). (iii) the draft’s “negation for every fact” hunch is NOT supported: cos(cross-term, per-layer write) distributions are broad and centered near zero (medians +0.07…+0.13 for layer 1) — a nearly orthogonal third channel, not an interference canceller (P3 refuted). Ablations: zeroing either block leaves only ~16–20% survivors; block 1 slightly more load-bearing than block 2 (P4’s direction refuted in 4/5 seeds — block 2 computes on the block-1-enriched stream).

F13b The expressivity wall: facts learned vs width

Trained on a fixed pool of 4000 random facts (seed 0). One block: 955 facts at H=20, then 1022–1026 for every width from 40 to 300 — flat to three digits across a 7.5× width range, including past H=210, the full quadratic span (210 monomials in 20 booleans). The plateau is the degree-2 function class itself, not parameters. Two blocks: 1244 → 1994 → 3522 → 4000 (the whole pool) at H=10/20/40/80 — width-limited below H=80, never expressivity-limited in range. Registered prediction P9 confirmed on both halves.

F13c Editing the 2-layer store: removal, injection, and the death of pull-out

The 2-layer model is still linear in its last block’s output map: logits = W x₁ + G h₂ with G = W D₂ and h₂(z) ∈ ℝ⁴⁰ the last block’s hidden representation — so the Part-2 KKT machinery transfers verbatim with h₂ as the stored-key frame. (i) Unlearning 10 of 1200 facts with the retain-aware C⁻¹-weighted edit: forgetting is exact by construction, but 516–536 of 1190 retained facts flip (~45%, median margin drop ≈ the entire median margin) — the same machinery cost 2/450 flips at Part-2 scale. The 40-dim frame is 30× overloaded; even the collateral-optimal edit destroys half the store. The 20-dim readout frame is 1.3–1.5× worse (P6’s 2× bar not met). (ii) Injection: 10 new facts land exactly (10/10, every seed) with 218–390 stored facts flipped — same order, slightly cheaper. (iii) Per-fact pull-out does not exist: the naive “component classifies its own key” metric saturates at ~100% (a whitening degeneracy of the 30×-overcomplete dictionary — a metric bug caught before claiming), while the honest component-deletion test shows every per-fact component is weightless: 0/1200 own-fact breaks, 0.0% median collateral, 0/1200 clean pull-outs. Facts in the composed regime are functionally present but have no addressable weight-space location. Class-level pull-out (a row of W plus both blocks) stays exact by construction.

Methods box — the KKT edit, one layer vs two

One layer (Part 2). The model is f(z) = D h(z), h(z) = (Lz)∗(Rz) — linear in D. To remove a fact, impose the linear constraint “f(z*) = uniform” on ΔD and, among all solutions, take the one minimizing ‖ΔD‖ in the metric C = Σ_k h(z_k)h(z_k)ᵀ over the stored keys. That least-norm-with-constraints problem is solved by its KKT conditions in closed form: ΔD ∝ (target − f(z*)) · (C⁻¹h*)ᵀ — rank-1, aimed along the direction the other stored keys use least. Collateral on every retained fact is exactly ΔD·h(z_j), predictable before applying (F11’s r = 1.000000). Baselines it beats: naive rank-1 subtraction of the fact’s component (fails to even forget — residual 23–68 logits — and flips 55% of retained facts, 9.2× worse); whole-unit ablation (catastrophic, units are shared); tensor-entry zeroing (F8: doesn’t remove behavior at all — diagonals co-carry).

Two layers (F13c). Composition does not break the trick, because the network is still linear in its LAST block’s output map: logits = W x₁ + (W D₂) h₂(z), everything upstream frozen inside h₂. Same machinery, keys h₂(z) ∈ ℝ⁴⁰, C = Σ h₂h₂ᵀ; the D₂ update is recovered as pinv(W)·ΔG and verified against the edited network (< 10⁻⁶ deviation). What changes is not the method but the geometry: 1200 facts crowd a 40-dim frame, so exact-forgetting edits necessarily bleed (~45% of the store), and injection (constraint: new label’s logit = best competitor + 1) is exact but costs 18–32%. The one thing with NO two-layer analog is per-fact weight-space pull-out — see F13c(iii).
